hardwood-flooring/venice.title: Hardwood Flooring Venice FL | Venice Island & Wellen Park
hardwood-flooring/venice.description: Hardwood flooring installers for Venice, FL, covering original heart pine in Edgewood's 1920s cottages and engineered hardwood in Wellen Park slab homes.
hardwood-flooring/venice.h1: Hardwood Flooring in Venice: Historic Cottages to New Slabs
hardwood-flooring/venice.lede: Hardwood flooring in Venice splits along a line most homeowners don't expect: raised wood subfloors on the island, poured slabs everywhere west of the Intracoastal.
hardwood-flooring/venice.capsule: On Venice Island's 1920s and 1930s cottages in Edgewood and the Venezia Park Historic District, a hardwood flooring quote starts with a raised-subfloor and crawlspace check, not a slab moisture reading, since original heart pine often survives under old carpet. Engineered hardwood fits Wellen Park's new slab construction better than solid nail-down. Typical 2026 installed ranges run $9-$19 per sq ft, with refinishing at $4.50-$7.
hardwood-flooring/venice.body_html:
Edgewood and the rest of Venice Island run on 1920s and 1930s wood-framed construction, which changes the whole hardwood flooring conversation before we even open a sample box. There's no slab to test for moisture on these lots; the house sits on a raised wood subfloor over a crawlspace, so the questions we ask are about ventilation, standing water history and subfloor condition instead of an RH meter reading. A surprising number of these cottages, especially the ones inside the 47-building Venezia Park Historic District, still have original heart pine or oak under a layer of decades-old carpet or vinyl tile nobody's pulled up.

A 1,050 sq ft Edgewood cottage built in 1931 would typically get a plank-by-plank inspection before we quote anything. If most of the boards read solid under a moisture meter and the finish coat is the main problem, sanding and refinishing usually wins over tearing the floor out, both on cost and on keeping the house's original character. Where the wood has rotted at exterior walls or a prior renovation nailed carpet tack strips straight through the boards, a full replacement, board-matched to what survives, is the more honest answer. Either way, the crawlspace gets a look first, since a damp or poorly vented one will undo a refinish within a couple of humid summers.

West of the Intracoastal, the calculus flips. Wellen Park's Gran Paradiso, Grand Palm and IslandWalk homes sit on slab, and solid nail-down hardwood isn't the plan there; engineered hardwood, glued or floated over the concrete, handles Gulf Coast humidity swings with less risk of the gapping and cupping solid wood can show on a slab. Inland golf communities like Pelican Pointe and The Plantation split the difference: mostly 1990s-2000s construction on slab, so engineered product is still the default when an owner wants a hardwood look rather than vinyl plank. Bay Indies, the 55-and-over manufactured-home community near Curry Creek, isn't a hardwood market at all; a raised chassis subfloor calls for a different product entirely, which is why we usually steer those estimates toward laminate flooring instead.

Whichever side of town the house is on, see the full Venice area page for the neighborhood-by-neighborhood breakdown, or read what we found on solid vs. engineered hardwood on a concrete slab before deciding which one fits your subfloor.
hardwood-flooring/venice.cost_html:
Refinishing sound original heart pine on Venice Island runs the same $4.50-$7.00 per sq ft typical 2026 range whether the house is in Edgewood or off the Historic District, so a 1,050 sq ft Edgewood cottage with restorable floors typically lands between $4,725 and $7,350, sanding, stain and finish coats included, well under what a full tear-out and replacement would cost on a house that size.

New engineered hardwood on a Wellen Park slab prices differently: a 1,600 sq ft Gran Paradiso great room and halls in a 7-9″ wide plank ($11-$15 installed) runs $17,600-$24,000, and jumps to $22,400-$30,400 for European white oak wide plank at $14-$19. Add slab self-leveling, $250-$700 per room, if the pour has more than the usual dip near an interior wall. The hardwood flooring cost guide lays out engineered vs. solid pricing, and the flooring cost calculator gives a same-day ballpark for your square footage.

faqs.q: Can original heart pine be saved in an Edgewood cottage?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Most 1920s and 1930s Venice Island cottages sit on a raised wood subfloor rather than a slab, and when the boards read solid under a moisture meter, sanding and refinishing the original heart pine typically costs less than a full hardwood flooring replacement.

faqs.q: Is solid hardwood a good fit for a Wellen Park slab home?
faqs.a: Not usually. Gran Paradiso, Grand Palm and IslandWalk homes sit on concrete slab, and engineered hardwood handles the humidity swings and slab movement with less risk of gapping than solid nail-down wood.

faqs.q: Does Bay Indies allow hardwood flooring?
faqs.a: We don't generally recommend it. Bay Indies is a 55-and-over manufactured-home community on a raised chassis subfloor, and laminate or vinyl plank rated for that subfloor type is a more reliable choice than hardwood.
